setup: Stand with feet hip-width, hinge forward to roughly 45-70 degrees holding a barbell with an overhand grip, spine flat.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back
Using momentum to jerk the bar up
Standing too upright, turning it into a shrug

formCues: Sit back onto the box, don't collapse down
Pause without relaxing at the bottom
Drive up through the whole foot
setup: Set a box or bench at or slightly below parallel height, position the barbell on the upper back, and stand in front of the box.
commonMistakes: Plopping down and losing tension
Rounding the back when touching the box
Rocking forward to stand up instead of driving through legs

formCues: Lower until rear knee nearly grazes floor
setup: Rest the top of the rear foot on a bench behind you, hold the barbell on the upper back, with the front foot far enough forward for a stable base.
commonMistakes: Placing the front foot too close to the bench
Letting the front knee cave inward
Pushing off the back foot excessively

setup: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand shoulder-width grip, arms extended, elbows close to the body.
commonMistakes: Swinging the hips to generate momentum
Letting elbows drift forward
Not fully extending at the bottom

formCues: Step back and across the body
Lower rear knee toward the floor
Push through front heel to return
setup: Stand with the barbell on the upper back, feet hip-width apart.
commonMistakes: Rotating the hips excessively
Losing balance from too large a cross-step
Letting front knee track inward

setup: Place heels on a small platform or plates, feet closer together than a standard squat, with the barbell on the upper back.
commonMistakes: Using too much heel elevation and losing balance
Leaning forward too much
Not controlling the descent

formCues: Drag the bar up along the torso
Keep elbows pulling back, not forward
setup: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip close to the thighs, elbows slightly behind the torso line.
commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift away from the body
Using shoulder flexion instead of a drag path
Swinging for momentum

formCues: Lower until triceps touch the floor
Press bar back up in a straight line
setup: Lie on the floor under a racked barbell or with spotter handoff, feet flat, gripping the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
commonMistakes: Bouncing elbows off the floor
Flaring elbows to 90 degrees
Arching excessively off the floor

formCues: Step forward and lower straight down
Push back to start through the front heel
setup: Stand with the barbell on the upper back, feet hip-width apart.
commonMistakes: Letting the front knee travel past the toes excessively
Taking too short a step
Leaning the torso forward

formCues: Soles of feet together, knees out
Drive hips up by squeezing glutes
setup: Lie on your back with the barbell over the hips, soles of the feet pressed together and knees splayed outward.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending the lower back
Using leg drive instead of glutes
Not achieving full hip extension

setup: Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip in front of the thighs, arms extended.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to lift the weight
Raising above shoulder height
Using too heavy a load and shrugging

setup: Rest the barbell across the front deltoids in a clean-grip rack position, elbows raised, feet shoulder-width apart.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows drop, causing the bar to roll forward
Excessive forward lean
Heels lifting off the floor

formCues: Hook grip or full clean grip on the bar
setup: Grip the bar just outside the shoulders in a full clean grip, rack it on the front deltoids with elbows high.
commonMistakes: Insufficient wrist flexibility causing elbow drop
Rounding the upper back
Losing bar contact with the shoulders

formCues: Cross arms over the bar to hold it in place
setup: Cross the arms in front of the body, hands gripping the opposite side of the bar to pin it against the front deltoids.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows drop and the bar slide down
Gripping too loosely
Leaning forward excessively

setup: Lie on your back with the barbell across the hips, knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart.
commonMistakes: Pushing through toes instead of heels
Hyperextending the spine at the top
Using a partial range of motion

formCues: Hinge at the hips with a soft knee bend
Push hips back as torso lowers
Stand tall by driving hips forward
setup: Rest the barbell on the upper back as in a squat, feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine
Bending the knees too much, turning it into a squat
Using too much load before mastering hip hinge mechanics

formCues: Keep torso as upright as possible
Squat down keeping bar close to legs
setup: Stand with a barbell held behind the body at arm's length, feet shoulder-width apart.
commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift away from the legs
Rounding the back to reach the bar
Rising onto the toes

formCues: Upper back braced on a bench
Drive hips up until torso is parallel to floor
Squeeze glutes hard at the top
setup: Sit with upper back against a bench, barbell padded and positioned over the hip crease, feet flat and knees bent.
commonMistakes: Overextending the lumbar spine at lockout
Pushing through toes instead of heels
Bench positioned too high or low for full range

formCues: Lower bar toward the neck/chin area
Blend triceps extension with a slight press
setup: Lie on a bench holding the barbell with a close grip, arms extended above the upper chest.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows out wide
Losing control of the bar path near the face
Using too heavy a load before mastering technique

formCues: Bar rests on rear deltoids, low on the back
Keep a moderate forward torso lean
setup: Position the barbell low across the rear deltoids just below the traps, feet shoulder-width apart, grip just outside shoulders.
commonMistakes: Bar creeping too high onto the neck
Knees caving inward on the ascent
Excessive forward lean losing bar path

formCues: Press bar in a straight vertical line
Tuck chin slightly as bar passes the face
setup: Stand holding a barbell at shoulder height with an overhand grip, feet shoulder-width apart, core braced.
commonMistakes: Overarching the lower back
Pressing the bar forward instead of straight up
Failing to fully lock out at the top

formCues: Lock the bar overhead with a wide grip
Keep the torso as vertical as possible
setup: Hold the barbell locked out overhead with a wide snatch-style grip, feet shoulder-width apart.
commonMistakes: Bar drifting forward of the mid-foot
Insufficient shoulder or ankle mobility limiting depth
Losing overhead lockout under load

formCues: Keep upper arms stationary and close to the head
setup: Stand or sit holding a barbell overhead with a narrow grip, arms fully extended.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows flare out wide
Moving the shoulders instead of isolating the elbows
Using excessive weight and losing control behind the head

formCues: Squat to depth and pause 1-3 seconds
Maintain tension, don't relax at the bottom
Keep torso angle consistent through the pause
Drive up explosively after the pause
setup: Set up as in a standard back squat with the barbell on the upper back, feet shoulder-width apart.
commonMistakes: Relaxing and losing tightness during the pause
Shifting weight forward while paused
Bouncing out of the bottom instead of a controlled drive

formCues: Set safety pins at desired depth
Lower under control to touch the pins
Drive up from a dead stop
setup: Set rack safety pins at the target depth, position the barbell on the upper back inside a squat rack.
commonMistakes: Crashing the bar onto the pins
Losing back tightness at the bottom
Setting pins at inconsistent height between reps

formCues: Rest upper arms flat on the preacher pad
Curl without lifting elbows off the pad
setup: Sit at a preacher bench with upper arms resting on the angled pad, gripping a barbell with an underhand grip.
commonMistakes: Lifting elbows off the pad
Not fully extending at the bottom
Using momentum to heave the weight up

formCues: Keep a slight elbow bend throughout
Lower bar back behind the head
Feel a stretch through the lats
Pull back over the chest using the lats
setup: Lie perpendicular on a bench with only the upper back supported, holding a barbell above the chest with arms extended.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows too much, shifting to a triceps movement
Lowering too far and straining the shoulders
Losing hip support and sagging

formCues: Press bar overhead using the leg drive momentum
setup: Stand holding the barbell at shoulder height, feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft.
commonMistakes: Dipping too deep like a squat
Pressing before the leg drive transfers upward
Failing to lock out overhead

formCues: Set bar at knee height or above on pins
Drive hips forward to lock out
Keep the bar close to the shins/thighs
setup: Set the barbell on rack pins at a partial height, typically at or above the knee, and grip it with feet hip-width apart.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back at the start
Letting the bar drift away from the body
Hyperextending at lockout

formCues: Grip bar with palms facing down
setup: Stand holding a barbell with an overhand (pronated) grip, arms extended, elbows close to the torso.
commonMistakes: Swinging the body for momentum
Letting elbows drift forward
Using too much weight and losing wrist position

formCues: Step backward and lower straight down
Push through the front heel to return
setup: Stand with the barbell on the upper back, feet hip-width apart.
commonMistakes: Taking too short a step back
Letting the front knee cave inward
Leaning the torso forward excessively

formCues: Rest forearms on a bench or thighs
Extend wrists upward against the bar
Keep movement isolated to the wrist
setup: Sit with forearms resting on the thighs or a bench, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, wrists just past the edge.
commonMistakes: Using the forearms/elbows to lift instead of wrists
Using too much weight and limiting range of motion
Rushing the eccentric phase

formCues: Keep back flat, avoid sagging hips
Roll out only as far as control allows
Pull back in using the core, not just the arms
setup: Kneel on the floor gripping a barbell loaded with small plates in front of the knees, core braced.
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back sag as the bar rolls out
Rolling out too far past control
Using the arms to pull back instead of the abs

formCues: Chest pinned to the bench throughout
Pull bar to the lower ribs
Avoid lifting the chest off the pad
setup: Lie face down on a raised bench with a barbell hanging below, gripping it with arms extended.
commonMistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench to cheat the rep
Using a partial range of motion
Yanking the bar instead of a controlled pull

formCues: Balls of feet on the platform edge
Lower heels for a full stretch
Press up onto the toes fully
setup: Sit with a padded barbell or machine resting across the knees, balls of the feet on a raised platform.
commonMistakes: Using a partial range of motion
Bouncing instead of controlling the stretch
Letting knees shift instead of isolating the ankle

formCues: Elevate shoulders straight up toward the ears
setup: Stand holding a barbell in front of the thighs with an overhand grip, arms straight.
commonMistakes: Rolling the shoulders instead of a vertical shrug
Using the arms/elbows to assist the lift
Using excessive weight and shortening range of motion

formCues: Bend directly to the side, not forward
setup: Stand with the barbell resting on the upper back or shoulders as in a squat, feet shoulder-width apart.
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso instead of a pure lateral bend
Using momentum to swing side to side
Bending too far and straining the lower back

formCues: Keep upper arms perpendicular to the floor
Lower bar toward the forehead/behind the head
setup: Lie on a bench holding a barbell with a close overhand grip, arms extended straight above the chest.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows flare or drift backward
Losing control of the bar near the head
Moving the shoulders instead of isolating the elbows

formCues: Lower straight down between the legs
Drive up through the front heel
setup: Stand in a staggered stance with the barbell on the upper back, front foot forward and rear foot back with heel raised.
commonMistakes: Stance too narrow, causing balance issues
Letting the front knee cave inward
Leaning the torso too far forward

setup: Stand with a light barbell on the upper back, feet shoulder-width apart, ready to squat and jump explosively.
commonMistakes: Using too much load, limiting explosiveness
Landing stiff-legged
Losing bar control on landing
